User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user account in the system, either a customer or an administrator. Does not store authentication credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The user's email address, used for communication and as a unique login identifier.

firstName.description: The first name of the user.

lastName.description: The last name of the user.

shippingAddress.description: The primary shipping address for the user.

billingAddress.description: The primary billing address for the user.

role.description: The role of the user within the system (e.g., 'customer', 'admin').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Represents a classification for products, allowing for organized browsing.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

name.description: The name of the category (e.g., 'Electronics', 'Home Goods').

description.description: A detailed description of the category.

parentCategoryId.description: Reference to a parent category, enabling hierarchical categories. (Relationship: Category 1:N Category)

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a single product available for purchase in the catalog.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

description.description: A detailed description of the product.

price.description: The current selling price of the product.

stockQuantity.description: The number of units of this product currently in stock.

imageUrls.description: An array of URLs pointing to images of the product.

categoryId.description: Reference to the category this product belongs to. (Relationship: Category 1:N Product)

sku.description: Stock Keeping Unit (SKU), a unique identifier for product variations, if applicable.

weight.description: The weight of the product, in a standardized unit (e.g., grams, kilograms).

dimensions.description: The dimensions of the product (e.g., 'LxWxH' in cm).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the product was added to the catalog.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the product information was last updated.

Cart.title: Cart
Cart.description: Represents a user's shopping cart, holding products selected for purchase.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Cart entity.

userId.description: Reference to the user who owns this cart. Can be null for anonymous carts. (Relationship: User 1:1 Cart)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the cart was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the cart was last updated (e.g., items added/removed).

CartItem.title: CartItem
CartItem.description: Represents a single product and its quantity within a shopping cart.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CartItem entity.

cartId.description: Reference to the shopping cart this item belongs to. (Relationship: Cart 1:N CartItem)

productId.description: Reference to the product added to the cart. (Relationship: Product 1:N CartItem)

quantity.description: The number of units of the product in the cart item.

priceAtTimeOfAddition.description: The price of the product when it was added to the cart, to handle price changes.

Order.title: Order
Order.description: Represents a completed or in-progress purchase made by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Order entity.

userId.description: Reference to the user who placed the order. (Relationship: User 1:N Order)

orderDate.description: The date and time when the order was placed.

totalAmount.description: The total monetary amount of the order, including shipping and taxes.

status.description: The current status of the order (e.g., 'pending', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled').

shippingAddress.description: The shipping address used for this specific order, captured at the time of order.

billingAddress.description: The billing address used for this specific order, captured at the time of order.

shippingMethod.description: The shipping method chosen for the order (e.g., 'Standard', 'Express').

paymentMethod.description: The payment method used for the order (e.g., 'Credit Card', 'PayPal').

trackingNumber.description: The tracking number for the shipment, if available.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the order record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the order record was last updated (e.g., status change).

OrderItem.title: OrderItem
OrderItem.description: Represents a single product and its quantity included in a specific order.

id.description: Unique identifier for the OrderItem entity.

orderId.description: Reference to the order this item belongs to. (Relationship: Order 1:N OrderItem)

productId.description: Reference to the product purchased. (Relationship: Product 1:N OrderItem)

quantity.description: The number of units of the product purchased in this order item.

pricePerUnit.description: The price of a single unit of the product at the time of purchase.

subtotal.description: The subtotal for this order item (quantity * pricePerUnit).

definition.description: Stores individual user profile information. Access is restricted to the owner (matching `request.auth.uid`) or administrators.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching `request.auth.uid`.

definition.description: Grants administrative privileges. The existence of a document for a specific `uid` in this collection indicates an administrator role, used for Database Access Control (DBAC). This collection stores no specific User data, only serves as a flag for admin UIDs.

params.name: uid
params.description: The unique user ID of an administrator, matching `request.auth.uid`.

definition.description: Stores product category information. Publicly readable for catalog browsing. Administrators have full read/write access.

params.name: categoryId
params.description: The unique identifier for the category.

definition.description: Stores product details for the catalog. Publicly readable. Administrators have full read/write access.

params.name: productId
params.description: The unique identifier for the product.

definition.description: Stores a user's shopping cart. The `userId` in the path (and in the document) must match `request.auth.uid` for authorization. For anonymous users, `userId` would be a temporary client-generated ID that is later updated on login.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user (or temporary session ID) who owns the cart.

params.name: cartId
params.description: The unique identifier for the shopping cart.

definition.description: Stores individual items within a user's shopping cart. Includes denormalized `userId` and `cartId` for authorization independence, ensuring `request.auth.uid` matches the `userId` in the document.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user (or temporary session ID) who owns the cart, inherited from the parent path.

params.name: cartId
params.description: The unique identifier for the shopping cart, inherited from the parent path.

params.name: cartItemId
params.description: The unique identifier for the cart item.

definition.description: Stores customer orders. The `userId` field within the document is used for ownership-based authorization, allowing users to query their own orders. Administrators have full read/write access to all orders.

params.name: orderId
params.description: The unique identifier for the order.

definition.description: Stores individual items within a specific order. Includes denormalized `userId` (from the parent order) and `orderId` for authorization independence, allowing rules to verify access without fetching the parent `Order` document.

params.name: orderId
params.description: The unique identifier for the order, inherited from the parent path.

params.name: orderItemId
params.description: The unique identifier for the order item.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support a robust e-commerce platform with distinct user roles (customers and administrators) and public catalog browsing, while prioritizing security, scalability, and debuggability of security rules. 

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
To achieve Authorization Independence, crucial authorization context fields are denormalized into subcollection documents. For instance, `CartItem` documents (in `/users/{userId}/carts/{cartId}/items/{cartItemId}`) will include both `userId` and `cartId` fields. Similarly, `OrderItem` documents (in `/orders/{orderId}/items/{orderItemId}`) will contain `userId` (inherited from the parent order) and `orderId`. This ensures that security rules evaluating access to these subcollection documents do not need to perform expensive and non-atomic `get()` operations on their parent documents, thereby simplifying rule logic and improving performance.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
Secure `list` operations (QAPs) are enabled through structural segregation and indexed fields:
1.  **Public Catalog:** `categories` and `products` are top-level collections, allowing for public, unauthenticated `list` and `get` operations. This inherently satisfies QAP for public data.
2.  **User-Owned Data:** `users/{userId}/carts` allows users to `list` only their own carts, as `request.auth.uid` must match `{userId}` in the path. Similarly for `cartItems` under their respective carts.
3.  **Orders:** `orders` is a top-level collection. Users can query their own orders using `db.collection('orders').where('userId', '==', request.auth.uid)`. This `where` clause acts as a server-side filter on an indexed field, making `list` operations QAP-compliant for individual users. Administrators, identified by a document in `admin_roles/{uid}`, will have permission to `list` all documents in the `orders` collection directly, as this is an explicit administrative capability.

**DBAC and Structural Segregation:**
-   `admin_roles/{uid}` collection is used for Database Access Control (DBAC). The mere existence of a document at this path for a given `uid` grants administrative privileges, making role checks explicit and efficient in security rules (e.g., `exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/admin_roles/$(request.auth.uid))`).
-   User-specific data like `User` profiles and `Cart` data are stored in `/users/{userId}` paths, providing strong, path-based ownership.
-   Public catalog data (`Category`, `Product`) is segregated into top-level collections for easy public access and efficient admin management without user-specific path constraints.
-   `Order` data is stored in a top-level `/orders/{orderId}` collection, with `userId` as an explicit field for ownership. This design choice enables both efficient user-specific filtering and global admin listing, fulfilling QAPs for different access patterns without requiring complex rule logic or mixing different security postures within the same *document* set.
